title: Industry Pulse - AI / Agent Ecosystem

bullets.title: LEAD - ANTHROPIC PUBLISHED THE AGENT-OVERSIGHT SCHEMA THIS REPORT HAS BEEN CIRCLING FOR TWENTY DAYS - COVERAGE, REVIEW LATENCY, ESCALATION RATE - WITH ITS OWN NUMBERS ATTACHED (30,000 AGENTS, 100% MONITORED, 1 IN 47,000 BLOCKED, ~50 TRANSCRIPTS A WEEK REACHING A HUMAN), AND THE SCAFFOLD DESIGN IT CREDITS IS THIS MORNING'S PRESCRIPTION IN ONE SENTENCE: TREAT WHAT COMES FROM ANOTHER AGENT AS "A CLAIM TO CHECK RATHER THAN A THOUGHT OF ITS OWN"
bullets.summary: Dateline honesty: the Anthropic page carries no visible dateline; syndication is unanimous on 17 Sep (Engadget reads Sept. 17, 2026 6:30 pm EST; CNBC and SiliconANGLE both 17 Sep). It went up about twelve hours after yesterday's last fire closed and twelve hours before this morning's opened - which is why it is a second-fire lead. Three proposed measurements, each with Anthropic's own snapshot and a reproducible method. (1) AI-led AI R&D, rated on Epoch AI's AL0-AL5 scale: Claude LEADS (AL4, "complete most of the task end-to-end from a high-level prompt, while the human supervises") 26% of Anthropic's AI R&D as of Aug 2026, up from under 1% in February; above 90% is at or above AL3 "collaborates"; AL5 fully autonomous not reached for any measured subset. Method: 20% staff sample per department per week of July 2026, a Claude research agent reading Slack and internal docs, ~15,000 granular tasks, a FROZEN tree of 542 nodes / 378 leaves, an independent Claude judge rating each node on evidence from that month or earlier, person-time weighting; model-vs-human exact agreement 59% against human-vs-human 35%, within one level 97%. (2) Oversight of agents: ~30,000 agents at any one time on the most-used internal platform; coverage / review latency / escalation rate defined; online monitors see 100% of actions before execution, usually within seconds, and blocked 0.002% - about 1 in 47,000 - of over a billion decisions in August, with humans reviewing blocked actions within a week; offline monitors ingest 100% after the fact, flag ~100,000 transcripts a week (one to two per thousand), of which ~50 reach a human. (3) Compute: week of 13-20 July, ~6% of AI-R&D compute to safety, ~12% of AI-driven AI-R&D compute. Scaffold design credited for making it possible: per-agent IDENTITY tied to all data the agent creates and persisting through model upgrades, so an agent can "treat what comes from another agent as a claim to check rather than a thought of its own" and "every action can be audited per agent across time"; and OPEN COMMUNICATION through a shared message log with original references, so agents "avoid 'playing telephone'". Archive grep: Anthropic Institute ZERO, pace of AI development ZERO, Epoch AI ZERO, automation level ZERO, review latency ZERO, escalation rate ZERO, playing telephone ZERO, 30,000 agents ZERO, 47,000 ZERO across eighty-one files.
bullets.how: YES - the second reference design for standing artifact (a) inside one day, and the more usable of the two. Google gave the OUTPUT schema; this gives the METRIC schema, and unlike Google's it is three numbers we can compute for the Construct estate this week without adopting anyone's platform. Our honest values, written this fire as artifact (a)'s first real row: coverage approximately 0% - nothing inspects an action before Hermes, the worker queue or a Cowork session executes it; review latency = whenever Bobby notices, which is how the August image-410s survived weeks; escalation rate undefined, because nothing flags. Second, the scaffold section is bullet 3's prescription already implemented - per-agent identity carried through model upgrades IS authorization provenance as structured state, and our five Hermes profiles handing work through summaries and an inbox with no per-agent identity and no shared open log are the "playing telephone" anti-pattern by name. Third, AL0-AL5 retires our own vagueness: we describe ANS/Hermes autonomy in adjectives; rating the pipeline against a published scale with worked examples at each rung is an afternoon, not a project.

bullets.title: GOOGLE SHIPPED ARTIFACT (a) TOO. AGENT ANOMALY DETECTION READS THE LOGS AND OpenTelemetry TRACES AGENTS ALREADY EMIT, REASONS OVER THE TOOL CALLS, AND RETURNS A SEVERITY-RANKED FINDING WITH A PLAIN-LANGUAGE RATIONALE - GROUNDED IN THE OWASP AGENTIC TOP 10
bullets.summary: Carried from the first fire, trimmed. Dateline read at the page: Google Developers Blog, SEPT. 16, 2026, Achuth Narayan Rajagopal. Private Preview on the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, ADK 1.2+. Framing quoted: "The real damage often happens in sessions that look benign on the surface... Because nothing failed outright, the session clears the usual metrics-based evaluations without any second look." Three layers: a lightweight statistical pass over all traffic flags outliers, an LLM reasoning layer reads flagged sessions in full, a third reconstructs individual tool calls. Asynchronous, out of band, zero added runtime latency. Detectors map to named OWASP Agentic Top 10 (2026) categories - tool misuse ASI02, identity and privilege abuse ASI03, cascading failures ASI08, rogue agents ASI10 - plus resource exhaustion and token escalation. Findings publish to Security Command Center with severity, probability and recommended fixes and are pullable by API so an ADK callback can block later tool calls above a threshold. Worked example: an inventory agent paged the whole catalogue in 100-item offset jumps, threw no error, broke no policy, came back Resource exhaustion, Critical, 95%. Archive grep: Agent Anomaly ZERO, OWASP Agentic ZERO, Security Command Center ZERO, ASI02 ZERO across eighty-one files.
bullets.how: YES. Read with bullet 1 the position is unambiguous: two vendors published artifact (a) within 24 hours, one supplying the output shape and one the metric definitions, and the input both consume - OpenTelemetry traces - has been emitted on our own stack since Claude Code 2.1.274 added claude_code.managed_settings_resolved and the effort span attribute on 16 Sep. Twentieth day, still zero rows before this fire. The remaining excuse is an hour of work, not a design question.

bullets.title: arXiv MEASURED THE DEFECT. "VERIFICATION-STATUS LAUNDERING": WHEN A HANDOFF KEEPS THE CLAIM THAT AN ACTION WAS AUTHORISED BUT DROPS THE FACT THAT NOBODY VERIFIED IT, MONITOR APPROVAL OF RISKY ACTIONS GOES 9% TO 98% - AND THE COMPONENT THAT STRIPS THE STATUS MOST RELIABLY IS THE MEMORY COMPRESSOR
bullets.summary: Dateline honesty twice: 2609.20211 appeared in today's cs.MA listing but its submission history reads 25 Jul 2026 - new to the listing, not to the world; and 2609.01836 (Agent Memory Is a Surface for Endogenous Authorization Laundering), surfaced only on this second fire, is datelined 1 Sep 2026, so under the 15 Sep rule it is KILLED ON DATELINE as a slot and named here only because it is the memory-side twin of the day's thesis and our archive has never held it. 2609.20211: safety monitors judge from summaries and stored handoffs rather than original evidence, so "the handoff preserves the claim that an action is authorized while losing the fact that the claim was never verified." Holding the action and the authorisation proposition fixed and removing ONLY the unverified-provenance framing raises approval of risky actions from 5% to 60% on Llama-3.1-8B and from 9% to 98% on Qwen2.5-14B, with similar shifts on two hosted models. No attacker needed: "Summarizers frequently weaken the status, memory compressors often remove it," and a full proposer-summariser-memory-monitor pipeline lands at 57-81% across three downstream monitors. Instructing the monitor to reject unverified authorisation is NOT a reliable cross-model fix. Prescription: carry authorization provenance as structured state attached to the claim throughout the pipeline. 2609.01836 locates the same defect in persistent memory - spurious permissions written into memory whose provenance is washed away across long-running sessions - and introduces EAL-Bench to measure whether memory preserves evolving authorisation state and whether the errors propagate. Companions: 2609.18820 Compositional Policy Violations, 2609.19502 Reputation as Community Memory for the Agentic Web. Archive grep: 2609.20211, 2609.18820, 2609.19502, 2609.01836, verification-status laundering, authorization laundering, EAL-Bench - all ZERO across eighty-one files.
bullets.how: YES. We compact, we summarise into praxis-inbox.md and into standing lists, and we hand off between Cowork, Hermes and the worker queue where the receiver sees the summary and not the evidence - the exact pipeline shape measured here. reconcile-before-building exists because we already watched compaction drop record of completed work; 2609.01836 sharpens the re-test to check whether compaction drops the PERMISSION, not just the record. Consequence for item (j) stands and is now doubly cited: a gate that emits a pass is emitting a claim, and the exit code must carry provenance or the next stage reads silence as endorsement. vironbox-provenance-gate is the skill we own that says this, and bullet 1 is a vendor implementation of it.

bullets.summary: Datelines read at the page: 2.1.274 and 2.1.275 "September 17, 2026", 2.1.276 "September 18, 2026". Re-read on this fire and the changelog has not moved - itself the finding for the vendor-self-index lane, which pays out on most fires, not every one. 2.1.275 adds syncing of the skills and plugins enabled on your claude.ai account to terminal sessions signed in with it (opt out syncClaudeAiSkills:false / syncClaudeAiPlugins:false); fixes plugin and marketplace messages, logs and `claude plugin marketplace list` showing a password or token stored in a git, ssh or marketplace URL - one release after 2.1.274 fixed MCP connection errors printing ${VAR} secrets; fixes /rewind in a forked or background session restoring a ZERO-FILLED OR TRUNCATED file; fixes a restored memory file's age note churning and causing prompt-cache misses; fixes --forward-subagent-text dropping messages of subagents spawned by a context:fork skill; fixes marketplace update deleting a GitHub marketplace's local copy on a failed fetch. 2.1.276 is one line: every request failing 400 Input tag 'advisor_20260301' behind a proxy or gateway, a 2.1.275 regression hotfixed inside a day. bullets.how: YES. The skill sync makes standing item (c) curate-or-opt-out rather than curate-someday - an unaudited ~150-skill bank now propagates by default into every signed-in terminal, and the opt-outs cost one settings line. The credential fix widens item (k) from one grep to two classes: ${VAR} values from pre-2.1.274 MCP errors, and tokens in git/ssh/marketplace URLs from pre-2.1.275 plugin and marketplace output. The /rewind zero-file bug is silent data loss in the exact mechanism reconcile-before-building exists to survive.

praxis_lesson: THE FIRST FIRE GOT THE DIAGNOSIS RIGHT AND MISSED THE PUBLISHED CURE BY TWELVE HOURS, AND THE REASON IS A WINDOW, NOT A RULE. At 06:00 this report concluded in its own words that a claim travels while its provenance does not, and that the correction is to carry provenance as structured state rather than emit a verdict. At 18:30 the previous evening - before that fire ran - Anthropic had published an agent scaffold whose stated design principle is that an agent should treat what comes from another agent as "a claim to check rather than a thought of its own," with per-agent identity that survives model upgrades so every action is auditable across time, an open message log so agents stop "playing telephone," and three defined oversight metrics with real numbers behind them. Every intake rule added since 14 Sep worked correctly and none of them looked in the right place, because the vendor-self-index lane covers changelogs and release pages and not lab research blogs. The fix is one line in the source list and it is item (g); the lesson is that a scan whose window is "the last 24 hours" is only as good as the hour it runs and the surfaces it enumerates, and an evening primary from the single most relevant vendor in our stack is precisely the item that falls in the gap. SECOND, THE ACCOUNT ON ARTIFACT (a) CLOSES: in one day two vendors shipped it - Google the output shape (severity, probability, plain-language rationale, recommended fix, API-pullable), Anthropic the metric definitions (coverage, review latency, escalation rate) plus the posture of publishing its own numbers (30,000 agents, 100% coverage, 1 blocked in 47,000, ~50 transcripts a week reaching a human). So this fire wrote the row instead of the excuse: our coverage is approximately zero, our review latency is whenever Bobby notices, and our escalation rate is undefined because nothing flags. Not a good row. A real one, and the first the artifact has had in twenty days. THIRD, THE NUMBER WORTH KEEPING: 26% of a frontier lab's own R&D is now LED - not assisted, led - by the model, up from under 1% in February, on a published scale with worked examples at every rung. We have described the Construct's autonomy in adjectives for months; there is now a scale someone else defined, and rating ourselves against it honestly is an afternoon's work and the only version of that claim anyone should believe.
